body: Christmas Island is a small island territory south-southwest of Java and an Australian external territory, counted as part of Australia for country streaks.
Coverage includes unique car coverage by a silver pickup truck with the visible truck bed, which helps identify Christmas Island.
Most of the island is covered by dense tropical forest, with some unpaved roads showing bright white sandy soil and areas with palm trees.
Christmas Island uses the standard Australian bollard: a white bollard with a red reflector on the front and grey reflector on the back.
Yellow licence plates are used on Christmas Island.
Coverage includes both regular roads and some very rural trails.
Built-up areas are mainly in the northeast; the rest is dense forest.
A boat trekker near the north coast follows the steep, rocky coastline with the white deck partly visible through the blur.
Numerous small trail trekkers cross the island, mainly through dense foliage but occasionally reaching beaches and lookouts.
The coastal Jln Pantai road is an exception with a trekker-only coverage without visible car parts.
The port area is identifiable by large cranes visible from many points.
A golf course trekker is found on the northeast coast, with Google car coverage on some parts.
Red crabs are famous on Christmas Island, with trekkers spotted among hundreds near Ethel Beach and The Dales; signs reference these crabs island-wide.
